No, Mr. President, Americans want Congress and you to do your job protecting humanity, protecting our utility bills, and protecting us from out-of-control, corrupt greed.

A principal role for government is to protect the American people. Safety must always be our first mandate. It is also the government’s job to protect the American people from unmitigated greed. The billionaires that you are listening to now would prefer the government stay on the sidelines. But the U.S. government knows how to regulate corporate greed and how to address new technologies that could destroy our world.

The robber barons of the Gilded Age amassed enormous fortunes while working families struggled. Soon thereafter, unchecked Wall Street speculation and a devastating stock market crash helped plunge America into the Great Depression.

President Franklin D. Roosevelt and Democrats responded with landmark reforms to rein in Wall Street, protect working families, and prevent another financial catastrophe. They established the Securities and Exchange Commission to police the stock market, created Social Security to provide economic security for Americans, and enacted the first federal minimum wage to protect workers from exploitation.

When we invented and exploded the atomic bomb in New Mexico in 1944, the scientist who oversaw it, J. Robert Oppenheimer, said, “now I am become Death, the destroyer of worlds.” He realized that this new technology could mean the end of humankind. After Hiroshima and Nagasaki, the United States, Congress, and our top scientists worked to limit the spread of nuclear weapons, even while many of the scientific inventions coming out of that discovery made their way into our business community and way of life.

What we do now will matter. We cannot just let AI and data centers regulate themselves or depend on their goodwill to lower utility costs and limit the most destructive possibilities inherent in this rapidly evolving technology. We must let local communities have a say in what is built in their neighborhoods so they can protect their water, environment, and cost burdens. 

But Congress must act. There must be a strong, enforceable national regulatory framework. We must have civil and criminal liability. We must protect the local and national financial interests of working families.

It is not a hoax, Mr. President. And we have a job to do.
